newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota corn harvest halted by heavy rain.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota corn harvest halted by heavy rain.

text.p: Heavy rains halted harvesting of corn in South Dakota early last week while high winds caused lodging in many fields, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in a report for the week to Sunday.
"Corn harvest was halted by rain early in the week which also delayed harvest completion of sorghum, sunflower and soybeans," the report said.

"Many corn fields were high in moisture content. However, the statewide hard freeze last week will help to dry down the corn," it added, noting the corn harvest was 59 percent complete, up from 56 percent a week earlier.
Corn harvest progress was slightly behind normal with the five-year pace standing at 60 percent.
High winds also caused lodging in sunflower fields.
The sunflower harvest increased to 90 percent complete, up from 85 percent a week earlier and the average of 85 percent.

Soybean harvesting was 98 percent complete, up from 95 percent a week earlier and ahead of the five-year average of 94 percent. It noted progress had been made "despite some areas being too wet from rain."
